rationale: The Latin anchors *cum fragore dissilire* (burst apart with a crash), *corruerunt* (they fell/collapsed), *rumpi* (to be burst/broken), and *frangi* (to be broken/shattered) all point to the core intransitive sense of physically coming apart or shattering. This matches break.v.02 ("become separated into pieces or fragments"), which captures the walls bursting/collapsing sense attested in the OE quotations.
